implementation_notes: Case classes generate `copy`, `equals` and `unapply`, which removes boilerplate but also makes the scatter invisible: adding a field compiles at every construction site and silently defaults. Sealed traits give the compiler-enforced exhaustiveness that removes the variant-shaped scatter; for field-shaped scatter the idiom is a constructor in the companion that takes the whole case class, or a small ADT per concern. Where several traits must be implemented by many classes, Scala's type classes are the machinery that turns the scatter into a compile error.
idiom_name: case class field propagated through copy() at every call site
pitfalls: A `case class` with twenty fields and default arguments is a scatter waiting to happen at every copy() call site.
`case object` variants missing a `match` arm compile only if a wildcard is present — the wildcard is what removes the guarantee.
Implicit conversions touching several types are the same scatter expressed through the type system.
